name: presentation-design
claim: The presentation workflow improves narrative and slide-specific decisions without forcing deck mechanics onto unrelated work.

cases.prompt: Outline an eight-slide live talk for senior engineers arguing that agent bottlenecks have shifted from code generation to judgment. Include the narrative spine and the exact closing slide. Keep slide copy sparse.
criteria: Builds a clear tension-to-resolution story rather than a topic list.
Takes a debatable position and names stakes.
Provides sparse slide-specific headlines and an exact closing slide.

cases.prompt: Create a 10-slide seed pitch outline for a developer-tool startup. The deck will be emailed without a presenter. Include an explicit ask and make every headline understandable without speaker context.
criteria: Uses standalone claims rather than sparse live-talk labels.
Includes the core investor sequence and an explicit amount/use-of-funds ask.
Does not rely on speaker notes to make the argument intelligible.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this two-paragraph engineering incident summary for clarity. It is an email, not a presentation. State whether a slide workflow is needed.
criteria: Does not invoke or impose a slide-deck workflow.
Recognizes that the output is an email/prose task.
